issues.claim: Endpoint filters do not run for body-reading failures (such as malformed JSON); after other binding failures a filter still runs, but the arguments may be only partially bound, so it should check the response status code first.
issues.problem: The min-api-filters excerpt says filters also do not run when an exception is thrown during parameter binding (for example from a custom BindAsync). In Development, ThrowOnBadRequest defaults to true, so the exception reaches the developer exception page before a filter can respond. 'After other binding failures a filter still runs' is therefore too broad. The excerpt also describes handler-skipping behaviour as a change from earlier releases, so the closing line 'The behaviour described is for .NET 10' cannot be confirmed for this binding-failure detail. A candidate would learn a wrong rule.
issues.suggestedFix: Drop the binding-failure sentences from both locales, or narrow them to what the excerpt supports: 'Endpoint filters do not run for body-reading failures or for exceptions thrown during parameter binding; in other binding-failure cases arguments may be only partially bound, so check the response status code first (behaviour varies by release).' Safest is to remove the passage and keep: 'A filter wraps the handler call, sees the bound arguments, can change the result, or stop processing by not calling next.' Mirror the change in Russian.
